claims.text: Monte Carlo simulations coupled with DFT-derived interaction parameters can model chemical short-range-order evolution in HfNbTaTiZr.
Chemical short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr specifically involves Hf-Ti and Ti-Zr clustering.
Hf-Ti and Ti-Zr clustering forms percolative pathways in HfNbTaTiZr.
Chemical short-range ordering alters the local vibrational dynamics of HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed percolative pathways act as preferential lattice-heat-transport channels.
Chemical short-range ordering enhances lattice thermal conductivity relative to a completely random HfNbTaTiZr configuration.
The proposed approach can accurately separate and predict lattice thermal conductivity over 300–1200 K.
The proposed model will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 20–30% relative to earlier analytical or DFT-based approaches.
Predicted lattice thermal conductivity will remain within ±20% of experimentally isolated lattice conductivity from 300 to 1200 K.
Earlier Debye-temperature-based analytical estimates and DFT simulations omitted chemical ordering.
Earlier approaches produced highly variable predictions.
Percolation effects relevant to HfNbTaTiZr thermal transport have been observed experimentally.
The approach is applicable to defect-free or near-ideal bulk HfNbTaTiZr samples between 300 and 1200 K.
The approach becomes less reliable below 300 K because lattice and electronic thermal-transport contributions interact or become difficult to separate.
Significant oxygen contamination reduces the applicability or reliability of the proposed predictions.
Electrical conductivity and Seebeck measurements can be used to isolate the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution for the proposed comparison.
